title: Letter from the Governor to Baroness Noakes DBE
summary: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey responded to the House of Lords Financial Services Regulation Committee's January 2026 report 'Private markets: Unknown unknowns', announcing a new Private Markets System-Wide Exploratory Scenario (PM SWES) exercise to test how the UK's private markets ecosystem might respond under stress. The letter reveals UK banks hold £173bn in banking book exposures to private market funds, equivalent to 8% of wholesale portfolios, and notes the FPC has lowered its benchmark for system-wide Tier 1 capital requirements from 14% to 13% of risk-weighted assets.
key_points: UK banks have £173bn of banking book exposures to private market funds and leveraged corporates backed by finance sponsors, equal to 8% of total committed limits across wholesale portfolios

The FPC is running a Private Markets System-Wide Exploratory Scenario (PM SWES) with participation from alternative asset managers, private equity/credit funds, banks, insurers, pension funds, endowments, and foundations
PM SWES will run in two rounds during 2026, with the final report published in early 2027
The FPC lowered its benchmark for system-wide Tier 1 capital requirements from 14% to 13% of risk-weighted assets, citing reduced systemic nature of some banks and improved risk measurement
Many major participants in the PM SWES are headquartered outside the UK, reflecting the global nature of private markets and openness of the UK economy
PRA has conducted a thematic review of private-equity-related financing activities, with banks providing responses on their risk management approaches
why_it_matters: This letter signals the Bank of England's increased focus on private market risks as a systemic concern. The £173bn exposure figure provides concrete data on bank-private market interconnections that could transmit stress across the financial system. The PM SWES represents a structured attempt to understand behavioral responses in private markets under stress—a first-of-its-kind exercise for this sector. The FPC's capital benchmark reduction reflects improved risk measurement and reduced systemic nature of some banks. Market participants should monitor findings as they may inform future regulatory capital requirements or supervisory expectations for banks' private market exposures.
macro_context: The letter responds to parliamentary scrutiny on private markets, an increasingly important sector that has grown significantly over two decades without being tested at current size by macroeconomic stress. The FPC's PM SWES and enhanced data collection efforts reflect regulatory concern about potential systemic risks from private market interconnections as the sector continues to evolve.
market_structure_context: The letter provides critical data on private market market structure: UK banks' £173bn exposure (8% of wholesale portfolios) connects traditional banking to the private markets ecosystem. The PM SWES exercise will examine complex interconnections between alternative asset managers, private equity/credit funds, banks, and institutional investors (insurers, pension funds, endowments, foundations). Many participants are headquartered outside the UK, indicating the global nature of these markets and cross-border data gaps that complicate monitoring. The PRA's thematic review of private-equity-related financing activities and banks' responses on risk management approaches further shape the supervisory framework for this interconnected system.
